patterns.name: memory-debt-cross-session
patterns.title: Memory Debt Cross-Session Enforcement
patterns.description: Hook on session-stop writes .memory-debt.md if semantic files empty; hook on user-prompt injects+deletes it at next session start — enforcement fires exactly once
patterns.context: Agents finish sessions without writing semantic memory files. Days later, a new session starts with empty decision-log, progress, and patterns — as if no work was done. Standard reminders in CLAUDE.md are ignored when the session never reaches that point.
patterns.solution: on-session-stop.sh scans decision-log.json, progress.json, and patterns.json — if all contain only baseline/template entries, writes .memory-debt.md with a timestamped debt reminder. on-user-prompt.sh at the very next session's first user message: reads the debt file, prepends its content to the prompt context, then deletes .memory-debt.md. Debt fires exactly once — no repeated warnings, no stale state across multiple sessions.

patterns.name: index-based-onclick
patterns.title: Index-Based Onclick for Data-Rich Cards
patterns.description: Store rendered items in a global array (window._safetyTabSessions); pass array index in onclick instead of serializing the full object to HTML attributes. Avoids encoding bugs with special characters in user-generated content.
patterns.context: HTML onclick attributes cannot safely carry arbitrary user-generated text. JSON.stringify + HTML-encoding attempts (replacing " with ") are fragile — any unescaped quote, newline, backslash, or template literal in the data silently corrupts the JS object literal. Bug is invisible: no console error, modal just opens blank.
patterns.solution: Before rendering cards, store all data objects in a window global array (e.g. window._safetyTabSessions = data). In each card's onclick, pass only the numeric index: onclick='openModal(${i})'. Handler checks typeof arg === 'number' and retrieves window._array[i]. Zero serialization. Works for any payload including user prompts, JSON objects, file paths with spaces, or code snippets.

patterns.name: backwards-compatible-schema-evolution
patterns.title: Backwards-Compatible JSON Schema Evolution
patterns.description: Add new fields as objects alongside old string fields. Use typeof checks in renderer to support both formats. Never break old data — migrate lazily on read, not on write.
patterns.context: A JSON field needs to evolve from a scalar (string) to a rich object (e.g. string → {path, added, removed}). Existing records use the old format. A migration script risks corrupting the only historical record — and may not be worth running for cosmetic improvements.
patterns.solution: Write new format for all new records going forward. Renderer detects format per entry with typeof f === 'object'. Objects get the rich treatment (heat-map, +N/-M display). Strings fall back to the legacy display (filename only). Old data is never touched. Migration is lazy and implicit — entries naturally upgrade as they are re-written by newer code. Only viable when the legacy display is still acceptable (degraded but not broken).
